course.title: ASP (Classic Active Server Pages) — From Beginner to Professional
course.description: A visual-first Classic ASP course for learning legacy IIS/VBScript applications, request/response processing, ADO data access, authentication and authorization, security, deployment, troubleshooting, maintenance, and modernization. This is Classic ASP, not ASP.NET.
course.version_scope: Classic ASP on IIS with VBScript (and limited JScript context). Microsoft Learn support guidance checked 2026-10-15 says ASP support follows the lifecycle of the host Windows operating system. Exact IIS settings, ADO/OLE DB providers, database syntax, COM components, process bitness, and third-party dependencies must be checked on the target host. Not a recommended default for new applications.
audience: Developers maintaining existing Classic ASP websites
Engineers auditing or modernizing older IIS-based systems
prerequisites: Basic HTML is helpful. Basic HTTP, programming, database, and Windows file/folder concepts are introduced as needed. A Windows test environment with IIS and Classic ASP is needed to execute examples; the CodeLeaf browser playground does not execute ASP.
learning_outcomes: Explain Classic ASP request execution through IIS and distinguish it from ASP.NET.
Write and inspect VBScript-based pages and handle HTML output safely.
Process forms and requests, manage cookies/sessions, and apply server-side authentication/authorization checks.
Use ADO connections, Recordsets, Commands, parameters, transactions, and cleanup patterns with provider-specific verification.
Audit and troubleshoot common security, IIS, COM, filesystem, database, performance, and deployment failure modes.
Document, test, refactor, and plan incremental modernization for a legacy application.
